What you are building

Use this page to connect the implementation back to the criteria you drafted at the beginning.

The key idea for this feature is Traceability between specification and evidence.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
Test caseOne measurable check of the system.
Expected resultWhat should happen if the feature works.
Actual resultWhat really happened during testing.
Evaluation evidenceProof used to judge whether the app meets the brief.

Why the client needs this

  • This is where you prove the app meets the client brief rather than simply feeling finished.
  • Evidence matters more than confidence.

Bring this forward from earlier pages

  • Open the success criteria and test plan side by side.
  • Make sure every major feature has observable proof, not just a vague claim.

How to treat the test table

  • One row should answer one question about the app.
  • Expected results must be observable.
  • A failed test is useful because it tells you what to repair next.

What counts as evidence

  • A visible task appearing after create.
  • A task disappearing after delete.
  • A status change still present after refresh.
  • A filtered list showing only the chosen records.

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • Evaluation is strongest when each criterion points to a specific test and result.
  • Testing should record evidence, not assumptions.
  • A good final review includes limitations as well as successes.

Evaluation mapping

Criterion
  -> test
  -> evidence
  -> pass / fail
  -> improvement note
Criterion

What the client needed.

Evidence

The screenshot, output, or observed behaviour that proves the feature works.

Pass / fail

This judgement should come from evidence rather than confidence.

Work through the evidence carefully

This page is about proof. Put the brief, the test plan, and the working system together.

Step 1 Test plan

Turn each criterion into an observed result

  • Run the feature, record the actual result, and decide pass or fail from evidence.
  • Do not write “works” without showing what actually happened.
Step 2 Project app

Capture evidence from the real build

  • Use the working system to prove create, delete, update, and retrieval behaviours.
  • Notice where the app still feels weak or unfinished.
Step 3 Evaluation notes

Finish with one honest improvement point

  • A real evaluation includes a limitation, not just celebration.
  • Tie that improvement back to the client brief or the testing evidence.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature
Test planHolds your measurable checksComplete actual results and pass/fail decisions
Project appProvides the evidenceCapture the behaviours that prove each criterion
Written evaluationExplains limitations and next stepsNote any unresolved weaknesses honestly

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • Each important feature maps back to a criterion.
  • Actual results are recorded rather than assumed.
  • Any gaps are identified honestly.
